title: Non-opioid chronic pain treatment
bottleneck: Chronic pain affects roughly 20% of adults, yet the analgesic arsenal is thin: NSAIDs carry cardiovascular and gastrointestinal risks, opioids cause dependence, and most neuropathic-pain drugs were repurposed from epilepsy or depression with modest efficacy. Pain's subjective, multifactorial nature defeats single-target drugs.
why_it_blocks: The opioid crisis was fueled by the absence of safe, effective alternatives; without them, pain care oscillates between suffering and addiction.
current_state: Non-opioid sodium-channel blockers newly approved for acute pain, anti-CGRP migraine drugs, and neuromodulation expand options. A broadly effective, safe chronic-pain drug class remains missing, and innovation incentives for non-blockbuster indications stay weak. Chronic pain's subjectivity makes clinical trials difficult, as placebo responses are large and endpoints are self-reported. Objective biomarkers of pain would transform drug development, but none is validated for routine use.
